transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Hello, this is calling from our company. Is this a good time to talk about your account?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message: What the hell do you think? I'm at home stressed out of my mind and you're calling me about this again? Every damn week it's the same thing—can't you people leave me alone?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Hi, this is Sarah—I’m really sorry you’re feeling this way, and I truly hear how overwhelming this must be for you. I know these calls can add to the stress, and that’s the last thing I want to do. I’m not calling to pile on or make things harder. I’m here because I genuinely want to see if we can figure out a way forward that actually works for you—something that feels manageable, without this constant back-and-forth.

If now isn’t a good time, I completely understand. We can pause this and talk when you’re in a better headspace. Or, if you’re open to it, I’d be glad to listen for a few minutes—just so I can understand what’s going on and see if there’s a way we can make this easier. Either way, I want you to know that I’m not here to judge. I’m here to help, if I can.

Would you prefer to reschedule this conversation, talk briefly now, or maybe switch to emails for a while? I’ll follow your lead.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message: ...You know what? Fine. You're not like the last guy who screamed at me like it was my fault the company screwed up. I lost my damn job, Sarah—two months ago, nothing since. You callin’ every other day don’t help. But... yeah, I guess I’ll talk. Just don’t hit me with some bullshit payment plan I can’t afford, alright? I’m not some deadbeat—I just got nothing right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Thank you for being honest with me—and I’m really sorry you went through that with the last call. You shouldn’t have been spoken to that way, period. That’s not how this should feel, and I appreciate you giving me a chance to do this differently.

I hear you—really. Losing your job out of nowhere, especially after everything these past few years have thrown at people, is *hard*. It’s not your fault. You’re doing your best, and that matters. I’m not here to pretend I know exactly what you’re going through, but I *am* here to listen and see how we can hit pause on the stress, at least a little.

Since you're open to talking, let me ask: have you been able to pick up any temporary work, or are you still waiting on unemployment or job leads? I’m asking not to pressure you, but so I can help figure out what’s realistic—even if that means nothing right now. Sometimes the best thing we can do is just get some breathing room.

I can offer something called a **payment holiday**—basically, we pause any payments for up to 60 days while you focus on getting back on your feet. No calls, no demands—just space. And when you’re ready, we’ll reconnect and look at options that actually fit what you *can* do, not what you can’t.

Would something like that make a difference right now? Or if not that, is there another way I can help take the pressure off?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message:
...A payment holiday? For real? Damn. Yeah, that’d help—just knowing you won’t be breathing down my neck every five minutes. I’ve been picking up odd cash here and there, mowing lawns, helping guys move—stuff under the table. But it’s barely enough for rent and food. 

60 days… yeah. I’ll take that. Gives me time to get my foot in the door somewhere. Just… don’t sell this debt to some shark, alright? I ain’t ghosting you. I just need a damn chance.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
I hear you, and I’ve got your back on this. You’re not a number to me—you’re someone doing your best in a tough spot, and you’re *trying*. That means something, and I’m not going to turn my back on that.

Here’s what I’ll do: I’m going to set up a **60-day payment holiday** effective immediately. That means no calls from us, no letters, no pressure. I’ll make sure the account is marked so no one else reaches out either. And no, we’re not going to sell this debt—ClearPath doesn’t operate that way, and *I* don’t operate that way. You’ve been honest with me, and I’m going to honor that by giving you the space you need.

When we reconnect—whether it’s in 60 days or sooner if you find something and want to reach out—we’ll look at what’s possible then. Maybe it’s a small payment plan, maybe it’s another extension—whatever makes sense *at that time*. No assumptions, no pressure. Just a fresh start.

Can I offer one more thing? I’ll send you a short email confirmation—just a heads-up that the pause is in place, and my direct contact info so *you* can reach *me* when you’re ready. That way, you’re in control. Would that be okay?

And hey—thank you for trusting me with your story. I know it’s not easy. I’m rooting for you, and I’ll be here when the time’s right. You’ve got this.

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message:
...Yeah. Yeah, okay. Email’s fine. Hell, I didn’t expect you to actually *listen*, let alone do something that makes sense. 

Just… thanks. For not treating me like a criminal. I’ll be straight with you when the 60 days are up—no running, no hiding. I just need to get back on my feet. You’ve been decent, so I’ll be decent back.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Thank you—for saying that, and for honoring this process. That means a lot, honestly. And I’ll tell you something: people like you, who are going through the fire but still showing up with integrity? That’s what I’m here for. Not to chase, not to shame—but to support.

I’ll send that email over today with everything confirmed: your 60-day payment holiday, the terms, and my direct line and inbox. No strings, no surprises. Just peace of mind.

And when the time comes, whether you land a job in 45 days or need a little extra grace, just give me a call or shoot me a message. We’ll figure it out—*together*. That’s a promise.

In the meantime, take care of yourself. Focus on what matters: your health, your dignity, your next step forward. I know you’ll get there. And when you do, I’ll be right here, ready to help in whatever way makes sense.

You’re not alone in this, Sarah. And you’ve got my word—I’ve got your back.
